# Set-ZbxActiveProxy

## SYNOPSIS

Changes how often a running active proxy session pulls its configuration.

## SYNTAX

```
Set-ZbxActiveProxy [-Name] <string> [-RefreshInterval] <TimeSpan> [-PassThru] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

The Set-ZbxActiveProxy cmdlet sets the -RefreshInterval of the active proxy session named in -Name while it keeps running, without losing the configuration it holds; the next pull follows the new interval. The interval is seconds or a time span. The command writes the session only with -PassThru, and -WhatIf shows the change.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Pull the configuration every minute

```powershell
Set-ZbxActiveProxy -Name 'uplink' -RefreshInterval '1m'
```

The interval takes Zabbix's time suffixes ('1m', '30s'); a number is seconds, and a time span works too.

### Example 2: Pull more often while testing, and show the session

```powershell
Set-ZbxActiveProxy -Name 'uplink' -RefreshInterval 5 -PassThru | Select-Object Name, Started
```

-PassThru writes the session after the change.

## INPUTS

## OUTPUTS

- `ZabbixActiveProxySession`: Represents an active proxy's uplink kept running as a session: it re-pulls the configuration on -RefreshInterval, over a ZabbixProxyUplink built with no DI container — the SDK type composes over a plain .
